answer: Epoch-Locked Behavioural Fingerprint. Each identity commits a hash of its interaction graph at epoch close; the next epoch must reproduce it within a tolerance, checked by random peers. A gale of inconsistent submissions triggers freezing. To farm many identities, an attacker must sustain matching fingerprints across every epoch, forcing real coordination work per identity. The atlas of tracked edges grows with age, so late sybils start behind. An opal-tier audit samples deep history, raising per-identity upkeep cost sharply.
